  "text": "“His winter coat. The brown one.”

The ferryman closed his eyes.

“What does that matter?”

“Was anything in the pockets?”

She remembered her mother standing beside the coffin, slipping something beneath the folded lapel. A kindness, Mara had thought. Something no one else needed to see.

“A letter.”

Below them, the wheel stopped. The sudden silence carried the soft tapping of wet paper against wood.

The ferryman put his cap back on, carefully, as though preparing to meet someone important.

“Then he’s come to deliver it.”

Mara lowered the mirror. In the tower, the light went out.

“Elias couldn’t read,” she said.

“I know.”

“No. Nobody knew.”

The ferryman looked at her then, and she saw that his collar was dripping. Water crawled from his cuffs and fell upward, vanishing beneath the sleeves.

Across the river, the tower door opened.

Mara could not make out the figure inside, only the brown shape of a coat and, below it, the familiar uneven stance. Elias had broken his ankle at eleven. It had healed badly.

She took one step.

“Ask him who wrote it,” the ferryman said.

The figure raised its hand.

“Who wrote the letter?” Mara called.

The answer crossed the water in her brother’s voice, breathless and irritated, just as he had sounded when she kept him waiting outside.

“You did.”

The brass mirror grew warm in her palm.

Behind its glass, where her own face should have been, Mara saw a desk, a sheet of blue-bordered paper, and her hand moving steadily across it.

She was wearing her mother’s wedding ring."
